current_date: Adopted May 2012 (cover text). Note: the council's current web page says it now uses the national validation criteria, so this 2012 list may no longer be applied.
current_evidence: The only adopted Bromsgrove local list found is the 'Local Validation Checklist' (cover: 'Adopted May 2012'), held as a 2012 Planning Committee appendix. Searches found nothing newer, and the council's live 'Submit a planning application' page links no local list and states 'The District Council uses the national validation criteria for planning applications'.

issues.detail: Grokbot's 'Validation list URL' is the generic 'Submit a planning application' web page, not a local validation list. Its 'Captured' status overstates what was found. The page itself says the council relies on the national validation criteria. The workbook should record 'no current published local list – national requirements apply', with the 2012 adopted checklist noted as the last local list, rather than presenting this page as the list.
issues.evidence: Page text: 'The District Council uses the national validation criteria for planning applications.' The only validation guidance linked is a plans-and-drawings note.

issues.detail: Grokbot did not find or mention Bromsgrove's last adopted Local Validation Checklist (May 2012), which covers 26 application types with 'all cases' and 'where relevant' requirements. It is badly outdated: it cites PPS3 (June 2011) and the 2010 DMPO, and the council website no longer links it. 'List date' should either note that this 2012 document exists and is out of date, or the row should state clearly that no local list applies. The current 'Undated' tells the user neither.
issues.evidence: Appendix 2 Adoption of Local Validation Checklist cover: 'Adopted May 2012'; refers to PPS3 (June 2011) and the 2010 DMPO.

issues.detail: All 5 tab_items under 'Submission rules' are process text, not validation requirements: (1) the administration fee for the Planning Portal service, (2) 'We have to send invalid applications back...', (3) the option to download paper forms from the Planning Portal, plus (4) and (5), two fragments about submitting 'Version one' and 'Version two' with and without personal details. Items 4 and 5 are cut from their context and do not say which documents need the two versions.
issues.evidence: tab_items texts, e.g. 'Please be aware that this service will incur an administration fee in addition to the planning application fee.'

issues.detail: Grokbot did not capture the council's linked 'Plans and Drawings to be submitted with a Planning Application' guidance note. Requirements: Location Plan at 1:1250 or 1:2500 (OS base, north point, red line including access to the public highway, blue line round other land owned); Block Plan at 1:200 or 1:500 (existing buildings, proposed works, trees, layout and landscaping); existing and proposed Elevations at 1:50 or 1:100 (all changed elevations; street scene images may be required); existing and proposed Floor Plans at 1:50 or 1:100; Tree Protection Plan where trees may be affected; Roof Plan if the roof is altered; Cross-sections if land levels change; Preliminary Ecological Survey where protected species may be affected; Heritage Statement where the building is of historic significance. These are the only local-style requirements on the current page and should replace the process text.
issues.evidence: bdc-plans-and-drawings-04-10-17.pdf: 'Location Plan (scale 1:1250 or 1:2500)... Block Plan (scale 1:200 or 1:500)... Tree protection plan, where trees may be affected... Roof plan, if the roof is to be altered... Cross-sections, if the proposal changes land levels.' (Undated in text; the filename suggests 4 Oct 2017.)

issues.detail: Both requirements in app_type_rows ('Archaeological Assessment / Desk-based Assessment' and 'Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) information / metric') are placed only under Full planning with an 'INFERRED' note. Every other type, including Householder, Outline and Listed building consent, shows '(none)'. The source applies archaeology to any site that does or may hold heritage assets with archaeological interest, whatever the application type. BNG is a national statutory requirement, not a local one. It applies to most full, outline and s73 applications (householder applications are exempt), so listing it only under Full planning misstates it.
issues.evidence: Page: 'Where a site includes or has the potential to include heritage assets with archaeological interest...'; 'for some planning applications, applicants are required to demonstrate 10% Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG)'.

issues.detail: The BNG trigger excerpt is cut off mid-word ('...(Modifications and Amendments) (Eng'). The archaeology excerpt drops the actual trigger condition: it starts at 'an appropriate desk-based assessment...' and omits 'Where a site includes or has the potential to include heritage assets with archaeological interest'.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows trigger_excerpt values compared with page text.

summary: Grokbot's link works but is a generic 'how to submit' page, not a local list. The council says it uses national validation criteria, and the last adopted local checklist dates from May 2012, which Grokbot never found. The captured tab items are all process text, and the only real requirement guidance on the page (the plans and drawings note) was not extracted.

The council tab and the app-type matrix therefore disagree about what was extracted.

withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: There is no inconsistency. 'Req. items' = 2 matches exactly the two app-type requirements (archaeology and BNG), and the five tab_items are 'Submission rules' process text that is not counted as requirements.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The two counted requirements match; the five tab items are process text.
